correctness.rationale: The edge-root directions span the zero-sum hyperplane, and central symmetry gives an interior origin. Its polar inequalities are exactly the centered Lipschitz constraints. Polar vertices give support-value-one facets, and the longest polar vectors are vertices by strict convexity. Central symmetry allows centering an arbitrary feasible ball at zero without loss of radius. Under the uniform independent coordinates the conditional variance sum weights each orthogonal Hoeffding term on A by |A| rather than 1. Equality forces all |A|>=2 terms to vanish. Centered additive terms are individually feasible and reconstruct a feasible sum for the sum metric; sharpness forces every term to be a factor maximizer. Uniqueness of centered factors gives the product contact count. Antipodal active inequalities force each optimal center to annihilate the contacting normals, and the gaps to finitely many remaining facets give a relative neighborhood in that annihilator. Sign differences isolate every lifted factor span, and distinct lifts are orthogonal; the codimension is therefore the sum of the q_i. For paths, the pairwise squared-distance variance bound is saturated only by the signed centered ramps, since the two endpoints must achieve their full distance. These prove the arbitrary finite metric and grid claims without extrapolation.
correctness.reproduction: python3 /workspace/review-evidence/frozen_math_crosschecks.py 5. Independently enumerated centered polar vertices using every possible tight spanning tree for two non-path examples. A three-point metric with distances (1,1,1) times the unit two-point path had max squared dual norm 17/6, 12 contacts, normal rank 3; distances (1,2,2) times that path gave 41/6, 4 contacts, rank 2. This uses connectedness of the graph of tight pairs at a vertex, because a disconnected tight graph would admit independent, small component shifts preserving centering. It is finite corroboration of the product classification, not an infinite proof. The frozen grid script was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: The scalar radius is covered by Bobkov–Houdré's maximal-variance tensorization and standard polarity; the Boolean-cube and path contact calculations also overlap exactly in their domains. The supported distinct claim is the full contacting-normal product classification and the affine rank law for all optimal centers for arbitrary finite factor metrics, and hence grid contacts beyond Boolean cubes. None of the inspected comparisons supplies that equality-case and geometric classification throughout this domain. Establishing it requires recovering all additive optimizers and proving the antipodal tight-normal span and local sufficiency; multiplying the scalar variance or using a total facet count does not do that.
residual_risks: The full earlier path proof and full formula of Higashitani–Jochemko–Michałek Theorem 3.1 were not inspected. The comparison does not establish exhaustive coverage or discovery priority; equivalent geometric formulations could occur under product spreads, Lipschitz-free spaces or symmetric edge polytope terminology.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of the origin contacts and a structural rank law for the translation freedom of all largest balls, not a scalar variance estimate or a recomputation of face numbers. It applies to arbitrary finite metrics and explains why path-product grids can have many facets yet relatively few contacts and a large affine incenter locus. It does not claim a complete description of the boundary of that locus.
